full_judgment: 2. The relevant fact, for the disposal of this petition in short are that the respondent Nos.1-10 as plaintiffs instituted the afore-said suit for declaration of their title and recovery of khas possession and for further declaration that Hiba-Bil-Ewaj deed No.614 of 1996 as described to the schedule to the plaint is void and the same not binding upon the plaintiffs alleging inter alia that the suit land originally belonged to Abu Sheikh C.S. record of right was prepared in his name in Khatian No.181. Abu Sheikh died leaving his son Shamsuddin and widow Rabizan. In S.A operation the same was recorded in their names. Shamsuddin transferred the land as described in schedule No.1, to the plaint to the other of plaintiffs and defendant No.1, Ayesha Akter by registered ewaj deed dated 23.01.1969 and delivered possession. Ayesha Khatun gifted 60 acre of land to the plaintiffs by beba-bil ewaj deed dated 25.08.1991 and delivered the possession. By amicable arrangement, the defendant No.1, got 20 acre of land as described in Schedule No.1, that is from the Western side of the disputed plot. Rabijan transferred 12 acre of land from plot No.927 to the father of the plaintiffs and Nur Habib by another heba-bil-ewaj deed dated 23.01.1969. Nur Habib transferred 12 acre of land of defendant No.1, by heba-bil-ewaj deed dated 02.08.1992 and delivered possession. Thus the defendant No.1, got 32 acre of land form plot No.927. One Goher Tarafder was the owner of the land as described in schedule No.3Ka to the plaint. His name was recorded in C.S. Khantian No.424. Goher Tarafder died leaving one son Nekbor Ali Tarafder who sold the same to Kariman Nessa Bibi by a deed dated 23.02.1950. The Government acquired .04 acre of land form the Schedule No. 3Ka to the plaint. Karimonnessa sold the rest. All acre of land to the plaintiff and defendant No.1, by sale deed dated 06.04.1978. Thus the plaintiffs got 06 2/3 acre and defendant No.1, got 03 1/3 acre from the Schedule No.3Ka to the plaint. By amicable Settlement, the defendant No.1, got the land from Schedule 1 Ka to the paint. The defendant No. 1, established a rice mill in 12 acre of land in plot No.927. He also got 12 acre of land from plot No.927 from his father, 20 acre from his Mother that is he acquired 32 acre of land from plot No.927. The defendant No.1, is brother of plaintiffs, defendant No.2, is his Nephew. The defendant No.1, taking permission from his father Nur Hbibi, established rece mill in 12 acre of land of plot No.927 and thereafter he constructed dwelling home-stead in the said 12 acre and started living therein. He got 12 acre of land from his mother by heba-bil ewaj deed dated 25.08.1991 and established rice mill in 12 acre of land. He sold his share of Keyotkhali Mouza on 04.09.1997 to Md Abdus Satif and Rajab Ali. The defendant No.1, created heba-bill-ewaj in respect of land measuring 14 acre of C.S. plot No.927 and S.A. No.2005 and 12 acre of plot No.927 and S.A. Plot No.2006 that is total .26 acre of land in favour of defendant No.2, on 08.09.1996 as described in schedule No.2, to the plaint. He forcibly entered into the said land on 02.07.1997, thereby dispossessed the plaintiffs. Thus the plaintiffs instituted other class Suit No.98 of 1997 for declaration of their title recovery of possession and permanent injunction in the court of Assistant Judge, Trishal, Mymensing and got an order of temporary injunction. The defendants, violating the said order of injunction, entered into .04 acre of land on 09.01.1999 again, thereby, dispossessed the plaintiffs from .28 acre of land out of .80 acre of plot No.927. On the same day they also entered into the possession of .20½ acre of land as described schedule No.1, (Ka) to the plaint. Hence was the suit.
